capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Page says “64.8 kWh high-voltage battery” without saying gross or usable; recorded as gross.

published_10_80_min.notes: “Approximately 43 minutes” on a Level 3 charger (>100 kW); the same page's FAQ says about 45 minutes.

consumption_highway_wh_per_km.notes: Test: ~75 mph (about 120 km/h) steady, ~14 C, dry, low wind, wheels not stated, battery-side vs wall-side not stated (article gives kWh per 100 km, probably car display) | InsideEVs 75 mph test of a Kona Electric Long Range (64.8 kWh, same generation and pack). Full-test figure 21.4 kWh per 100 km = 214 Wh/km (first 33 mi 20.3, midpoint 20.5 kWh/100 km). 132 mi driven with 18 % left. Test car was a 2024 (same generation and pack). Wind at his back on the first leg, against on the return.

charge_port.notes: Hyundai Canada FAQ names the 2026 KONA Electric as an EV with a CCS port that can use a NACS adapter available separately.

supercharger_access.notes: Per the same FAQ, with a NACS adapter (sold separately; Hyundai Canada EV hub also advertises a free CCS-to-NACS adapter offer until 2026-12-31 for eligible native-CCS EVs, model list not shown).
